PP-008.text:
Founded in 2008, Start2 Group has grown into a global leader in accelerator design, program methodology, and scale-up support, with over 130 employees worldwide and a network of more than 1,300 expert and industry mentors. Recognized by Financial Times as one of the top Startup Hubs, and by CB Insights as one of the top startup accelerators for German Accelerator, Start2 Group's experience spans four continents, with over 6,000 startups supported across 15+ long-term accelerator programs ranging from early-stage ventures to international expansion. This track record is underpinned by a methodology proven across numerous government-backed and private sector initiatives.

Start2 Group accompanies and shapes the entire innovation journey, from initial idea to global scaling. The organization coaches startups and corporate teams to develop ideas into viable products, then supports them in launching and scaling their companies domestically and internationally. Start2 Group also connects key innovation stakeholders to accelerate innovation, including through corporate-startup partnering and investor-startup matching.

To date, more than 6,000 startups have benefited from Start2 Group's programs, with notable success stories including European unicorns Flixbus, Celonis, Forto, Signavio, Auto1 Group, Staffbase, and N26, among others. The breadth of startups supported spans diverse industries, including Fintech, Energy & Cleantech, Edutech, Health & Life Sciences, DeepTech (AI/ML, Data, Quantum, Cybersecurity), Enterprise SaaS, and AgriTech, among others. Start2 Group is experienced in delivering both industry-agnostic and industry-specific programs, and through its global competence centers for Artificial Intelligence, Climate Tech, and Life Sciences, offers specialized support for technology companies and scale-ups.

Beyond supporting startups directly, Start2 Group also organizes and hosts its own recurring investor ecosystem event, Cashwalk, which connects high-potential startups with funding from venture capital and angel investors. Across 16 editions to date, Cashwalk has attracted an average of more than 50 investors per event.

PP-009.text:
Start2 Group’s programs are conducted in leading innovation centers worldwide, leveraging our global teams and network. Start2 Group maintains a presence across 20 markets globally, combining a network of 15 offices with teams operating in an additional five markets.

In Asia, Start2 Group operates offices in Singapore, Bangalore, Seoul, Tokyo, and Shanghai, with additional teams based in Manila and Saigon.

In North America, the firm has offices in Silicon Valley, Boston, New York, Boulder, and Miami, supported by teams in Dallas and Austin. In South America, the firm maintains offices in Buenos Aires and Sao Paulo.

In Europe, Start2 Group operates offices in Munich, Berlin, and Dusseldorf, with a further team presence in London.

This footprint enables Start2 Group to combine deep local market knowledge with the ability to coordinate and deliver projects across regions and time zones.

PP-012.text:
Over the years, Start2 Group has operated numerous startup accelerators, international scaling programs, and investor events on behalf of government and corporate clients, reflecting the depth of its experience in providing holistic acceleration and scaling support. The ecosystems built through these initiatives create sustained opportunities for growth and impact, offering a proven approach tailored to the distinct challenges startups face at each stage of their journey.

Start2 Group is highly experienced in holding acceleration programs on a global scale and have a proven track record of being a trusted partner to foreign entities and governments from Europe, Asia and the Americas:

1. **Southeast Asia Regional Program on Combating Marine Plastics **(SEA-MaP) is a flagship initiative of ASEAN, financed by the World Bank, focused on preventing land- and sea-based marine plastic pollution across Southeast Asia. As the Accelerator partner for the Regional Platform for Innovation and Investments (IIP), Start2 Group connects startups with corporates such as Mondelez, Mr. DIY, and 7 Bridges, facilitates end-to-end corporate pilots, equips startups to expand and grow, strengthens corporates' capacity to adopt innovation, and creates follow-on opportunities for startups beyond the pilot stage.
2.** Scaler8** is a platform operated by Start2 Group that has supported more than 120 startups and SMEs globally in exploring, preparing for, and accessing new markets across Asia, Europe, and North and South America, through bespoke international expansion strategies and demand-driven, cross-border open innovation. Key public-sector partners powering the program include the Malaysian Research Accelerator for Technology & Innovation (MRANTI), Enterprise Singapore, the Economic Development Board of Singapore, the Korean Institute of Startup & Entrepreneurship Development (KISED), and the Tokyo Metropolitan Government.
3. **German Accelerator,** ranked 14th most successful accelerator globally by CB Insights, has been operated by Start2 Group since its inception in 2012 on behalf of the German Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Energy. This global program has supported more than 1,600 German startups and scale-ups to date, including leading deep-tech success stories such as Forto and Signavio, collectively helping them unlock \$17 billion in funding since program participation. The program targets leading innovation hubs across more than 20 markets in North and South America and Asia-Pacific, with recent expansion into Africa, and now supports more than 400 German startups annually across 44 cohorts, fostering internationalization through structured mentorship and sector-specific guidance. More than 700 startups have joined its virtual-first Kickstart program, which runs approximately 15 cohorts per year focused on early international expansion education.
4.** Scale-up.NRW** helps successful startups from North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany's largest state, scale globally while creating a pull-up effect for the broader regional startup ecosystem. The program supports North Rhine-Westphalia's ambition to become a European top-10 startup region by 2025 and is commissioned by the State's Ministry of Economic Affairs, Industry, Climate Action and Energy.

Building on this track record, Start2 Group has supported startups of numerous nationalities through its startup acceleration and internationalization programs. With this support, these companies have entered new markets with validated market hypotheses, refined go-to-market strategies, and strengthened regional networks, becoming credible partners to the corporates and institutions they engage with. Their continued traction reflects a repeatable pattern: startups that progress through Start2 Group's methodology are structurally better prepared to scale, engage enterprise and government stakeholders, and deliver on pilots and proofs of concept in complex international markets.

PP-018.text:
Climate Tech is one of Start2 Group's competence centers, with a focus across four areas: circular economy, agrifood tech, energy and decarbonization, and smart and sustainable cities. The competence center drives impact through three key initiatives:
1. startup acceleration, which prepares climate-tech startups to become market-ready and investable;
2. open innovation, which matches pressing climate challenges with breakthrough solutions across the region and facilitates co-creation; and
3. ecosystem engagement, which strengthens the regional climate tech ecosystem through high-impact events, thought leadership, and strategic partnerships.

Over the past eight years, Start2 Group has supported the scaling of over 100 climate tech startups across Asia. This includes dedicated climate tech programs, such as the Southeast Asia Regional Program on Combating Marine Plastics (SEA-MaP), delivered in partnership with the World Bank and ASEAN, as well as broader programs such as German Accelerator and Scaler8 that also serve climate tech ventures. Under SEA-MaP, now completed last August 2026, Start2 Group operated the Regional Platform for Innovation and Investments, generating eleven (11) corporate-startup matches for Climate Tech ventures across three cohorts, including corporates such as SM, Mondelez, Vivo Barefoot, and SCGC.

Alongside its acceleration and open innovation work, Start2 Group has strengthened the climate tech ecosystem in Asia through events run in partnership with leading regional and international institutions, including Enterprise Singapore, the Ministry of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs (South Korea), GIZ (Philippines), the Infocomm Media Development Authority (Singapore), and the United Nations Development Programme (Vietnam).

PP-038.text:
Every session in a Start2 Group program is designed based on the objectives of the program. Before any session is built, Start2 Group evaluates the needs of each startup and the target objective of each session: a knowledge transfer, a framework they can apply immediately, a concrete business outcome, or a rehearsed skill such as a pitch or a sales approach. That outcome determines the format.

Start2 Group employs a variety of session formats, intentionally designed for the target outcomes of the program:

• **Masterclasses**: This type of session is used for specialized, theory-heavy topics where deep knowledge transfer is the objective.
• **Workshops**: This type of session blends theory with hands-on application, giving participants a sandbox to test new skills before using them in the real market.
• **Pitch Tanks:** This session puts founders in front of 2-3 investors mock capital to deploy, in a live Shark Tank-style format that pressure-tests both the pitch and the business case.
• **Pitch Training: **This session** **pairs a startup with an expert pitch mentor for focused, individual coaching for material effectiveness, pitch delivery, and overall communication approach.
• **Business Meetings and Mentor Sessions**: Where the goal is direct business outcomes, we run curated one-on-one business meetings and mentor sessions, matching each startup with mentors suited to their domain or target market
• **Site Visits**: Organized trips to offices or sites of ecosystem partners, innovation hubs, corporates, and government bodies for direct market immersion.

Most sessions typically run in 60, 90, or 120 minute blocks, delivered virtually or in person depending on the program's format and the outcome each session is built to achieve.

PP-039.text:
** 1. Recruitment Funnel **
Start2 Group expects the funnel to run from approximately four hundred raw applications, to roughly one hundred and twenty quality applications across the confirmed Focus Areas, down to twenty startups confirmed and onboarded as the final cohort. These figures are Start2 Group's working estimate and will be confirmed with *\[to-update client name\] *once the Focus Areas are set.

2. **Multi-Channel Sourcing **
The applicant pool is built from four channels working together, supporting a parallel scouting and sourcing approach. Sourcing is a highly targeted approach where Start2 Group will specifically reach out to startups with a strong fit in profile and problem-solution fit. Scouting is a broad-based approach to reach out to as many relevant startups as possible, using multipliers, partners and marketing campaigns. Together, the two balance precision and reach. Sourcing surfaces startups that are a strong fit from the outset, while scouting builds a wide, diverse pool that also captures motivated startups who self-select into the program through open applications.

Sourcing approach:
• **Alumni and network referrals: **candidates from Start2 Group's own program alumni and mentor referrals, and from Start2 Group's accelerator and corporate venture partner network built up across earlier FutureTech cohorts and other regional mandates.
• **Glassdollar AI-powered database of over 20 million startups (to-update refer to 5.0): **structured secondary research using Dealroom for founding year, funding stage, and traction data, together with Glassdollar's venture clienting platform, a database of over twenty million companies that surfaces non-obvious, early stage, and specialized startups beyond the well-known names.

Scouting approach:
• **Multipliers and partners: **sourcing anchored in the target market through Start2 Group’s existing strategic partners, such as *\[to-update partners in target market\].* Other multipliers in other countries such as SGInnovate (Singapore), JETRO (Japan), A\*STAR (Singapore), Seoul Startup Hub (Korea) will also be engaged to support with sourcing.
• **Marketing and outreach: **targeted marketing and LinkedIn outreach to scout founders directly, alongside open calls for applications.


3. **Criteria-Based Shortlisting **
All candidates are logged and scored in a dedicated CRM against a weighted model built around *\[to-update client name\]’s *own published program criteria:

*\[to-update INSERT CLIENT-REQUIRED CRITERIA\]*

Apart from the pre-requisite criteria provided by *\[to-update client name\]*, Start2 Group also recommends the following criteria:
• Strategic fit between the solution of the startup and the challenge statements: alignment on technology need, portfolio complementarity, and timing
• Mutual value creation potential: assessing what each side stands to gain (commercial revenue, technology access, market credibility, investment upside) so the match is durable rather than one-sided.
• Market entry feasibility: practical assessment of regulatory, logistical, and commercial barriers to the startup actually operating in the target market within a realistic timeframe.
• Cultural and operational alignment: compatibility in culture / working style and risk appetite between startup and corporate, which in practice determines whether a promising match converts into a working relationship.

4. **Structured Delivery **
Based on the agreed selection criteria, shortlists are then delivered to Challenge Owners in a standardized format, covering startup name, location, funding stage, technology, and proven client or traction record, so that Challenge Owners can evaluate fit quickly.

Start2 Group has applied this same model successfully across several corporate scouting mandates in the region, including Mann+Hummel Open Innovation Challenge 2026, Aumovio, Liebherr and more.

5. *\[to-update For Corporate Proposals\] ***The Glassdollar Partnership **

Glassdollar is a venture clienting platform that lets corporates systematically source and evaluate startup partnerships against a defined need, and it forms an additional layer in Start2 Group's scouting methodology. Since March 2026, Start2 Group and Glassdollar have operated as one delivery partnership for venture clienting globally: Glassdollar contributes sourcing intelligence, its database, and its record of thousands of completed proof of concepts, while Start2 Group leads implementation, scoping, and pilot delivery on the ground across its markets. Glassdollar's own service team is transitioning into Start2 Group as part of this alliance, so a corporate partner works with one continuous process, from sourcing through pilot delivery.

Applied to *\[to-update program name\]*, this means the sourcing step described above draws on more than Start2 Group's own network and secondary research. It draws on a live partnership with a platform purpose built for matching startups to a defined corporate challenge, giving Challenge Owners access to non-obvious, specialized, and early stage startups outside Start2 Group's existing alumni and mentor pool.

PP-065.text:
Recognizing that program requirements, participant numbers, and delivery needs may evolve throughout the program, Start2 Group has established a flexible delivery model that enables timely adjustments while maintaining program quality and consistency.

*\[For programs that require long-term engagement\] ***Flexibility in the Delivery Team **
The delivery structure is designed to accommodate changes in workload and team availability without disrupting program implementation. This is supported by:
• A clearly defined team structure with designated leads and deputies for key functions, ensuring continuity of responsibilities.
• Cross-functional knowledge sharing and documentation to minimize dependency on individual team members.
• The ability to reallocate resources across activities in response to changes in workload or delivery priorities.
• Access to additional internal or external resources, where required, to address temporary increases in workload or specialized needs.
• Reserve pool of pre-vetted external experts with freelance mentoring agreements with the contractor who can be mobilized in short-order.

Any internal changes to the delivery team will be managed by *\[to-update the Program Lead\]*, who will assess their potential impact on timelines, deliverables, quality, and KPIs and implement appropriate mitigation measures. The *\[to-update client name\] *will be informed of material changes where relevant.

**Scalability of Program Delivery **
The program delivery model is designed to scale up or down according to participant numbers and evolving program requirements, while maintaining a consistent participant experience and quality standard. This flexibility will be enabled through:
• Modular program activities that can be expanded, reduced, or adapted according to participant volumes.
• Flexible cohort sizes and delivery formats to accommodate different levels of participation.
• Scalable use of digital and hybrid delivery methods where appropriate.
• Adjustment of facilitator, mentor, expert, and operational resources in line with participant demand.
• Prioritization and sequencing of activities where changes in volume or timing require adjustments to the implementation plan.
